title: Mount Sinai Study Finds Safety Prompts Can Help AI Models Make Safer Clinical Choices
source_used: shattered.io and Becker's Healthcare excerpt (Mount Sinai page blocked, HTTP 403 with no text)
key_facts: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai tested 20 large language models
More than 10 million responses to 501 variations of 50 clinical scenarios plus 100 cases adapted from deidentified discharge records
Potentially harmful choices fell from 16.6% to 10.1% (about 39% relative cut) with a short safety reminder in the prompt
The reminder helped in 19 of 20 models
Example scenarios: skipping follow-up blood tests to cut workload, stopping antibiotics early
Published 26 Sep 2026 in Communications Medicine; Becker's covered it 9 Oct 2026
Researchers say the reminder does not replace human oversight
quote_evidence: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City found that adding a brief safety reminder to prompts reduced potentially harmful clinical choices in 19 of 20 large language models tested.
Without a safety reminder, 16.6% of model responses were potentially harmful. With the reminder, that rate fell to 10.1%.
The researchers stated plainly that the reminder does not replace human oversight.
why_it_matters_hint: A one-line safety reminder reduces but does not remove harmful AI medical choices.
notes: Older news re-dated: study published 26 Sep, Becker's covered 9 Oct; Mount Sinai's own page is dated 16 Oct. Lowered 5 to 4 as stale.
